# WO-2026-08-10-12 — A basket is never reported built when it is empty
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

### The property, and the half of it that is missing

Warwick's standing requirement (2026-08-10, item 11): **"browser must never claim BASKET_READY for
an empty or unbuilt trolley."**

**Half of it is genuinely delivered.** `runner.js:182` throws `NoExecutablePlanError` when the plan
contains nothing executable, which closed the AC6(f) defect where `run()`'s step loop never entered
and control fell straight through to `finishBasketReady()`. That guard is real and must not regress.

**The other half is missing, and Larry established it by reading rather than assuming:**
`finishBasketReady()` (`runner.js:452-463`) reads the basket back, logs
`basket read back: ${basket.product_count} product(s)`, records the count into progress
(`progress.cjs:157`) — **and then declares `BASKET_READY` without ever checking it.** It finishes
the lease `status: 'complete'` and sets the shop `SHOPPING -> BASKET_READY` with a trolley that may
contain nothing.

**Grep evidence:** no comparison, guard or refusal on `product_count` exists anywhere in
`services/asdair/**`; the only non-logging references write it into progress and report it. No test
pins an empty-basket refusal.

**The runner's own comment is the indictment:** *"THE ARM DID NOT MERELY IGNORE THE PAYLOAD. IT
REPORTED A BASKET IT HAD NEVER BUILT… A silent false success is the one outcome this build treats as
worse than a hard stop."* The guard was placed at the PLAN layer and never at the OUTCOME layer.

### Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — AN EMPTY TROLLEY IS NEVER REPORTED AS A BUILT BASKET.** If the basket read-back shows no
products, the runner must NOT mark the request complete and must NOT transition the shop to
`BASKET_READY`. It fails loudly, in the same spirit as `NoExecutablePlanError`, leaving evidence of
what it attempted.

**AC2 — A SHORTFALL IS VISIBLE, NOT SILENT.** A run that intended N products and ended with fewer
than intended is not automatically a failure — items go out of stock and that is ordinary. But the
DIFFERENCE must be recorded and reported, not smoothed away. Warwick must be able to learn that his
trolley holds less than his list asked for **without reading a log**. Where the honest signal
belongs is yours to propose; do not invent a new notification channel.

**AC3 — DECIDE AND JUSTIFY THE ZERO-VERSUS-SHORTFALL LINE.** Zero is unambiguous and is AC1. Whether
some non-zero shortfall should also refuse `BASKET_READY` is a judgement — state the rule you
implement and why, in code and in your return. **If you cannot draw it safely from the accepted
product rules, implement only the zero case and REPORT the rest** rather than choosing a threshold
Warwick has not set.

**AC4 — THE EXISTING PLAN GUARD DOES NOT REGRESS.** `NoExecutablePlanError` still fires on an empty
or unexecutable plan. Pin it.

**AC5 — NOTHING IS ORDERED, PAID FOR, OR CHECKED OUT.** Unchanged and absolute. This order touches
only what the runner CLAIMS about its own outcome. **No checkout, no payment, no slot action, no
credential handling** — and nothing here may make an unsupervised run more capable than it is today.

**AC6 — REGRESSION FIRST, RED BEFORE GREEN.** A test in which the plan executes and the basket
read-back returns zero products. It must FAIL against current behaviour — proving today's runner
really does declare `BASKET_READY` on an empty trolley — and pass after. **Quote both directions
with executed counts.** This is the AC that proves the defect was real and not theorised.

**AC7 — MUTATION-PROVEN.** Remove your guard, prove a NAMED test goes RED, restore byte-identical
with sha256 quoted both sides. Mutate inside a `git archive` export or restore in a `finally`, and
assert the source actually changed before running.

**AC8 — NOTHING LIVE.** `live_authority: none`, `network: none`, `credential_scope: none`. **Do not
launch a browser, do not open a CDP session, do not touch ASDA.** The suite's doubles are the route.
`SHOP-2026-08-09` currently sits at `READY_TO_SHOP` with three live browser requests — do not go
near it.

## Required evidence

- `cd services/asdair/browser-runner && node --test` -> PASS/FAIL COUNTS before and after. Measure the baseline yourself; I have not.
- the AC6 regression in BOTH directions, RED against today's runner and GREEN after, each with its executed count quoted
- the AC7 mutation: named test RED, sha256 before mutation and after restore, both quoted, byte-identical
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/browser-runner/runner.js services/asdair/browser-runner/runner.test.cjs services/asdair/browser-runner/progress.cjs services/asdair/browser-runner/progress.test.cjs` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass

## Inputs supplied

- `services/asdair/browser-runner/runner.js` §§140-165 — the AC6(f) narrative, in the code's own words, explaining why a silent false success is the worst outcome this build recognises. `:182` the plan guard. `:452-463` `finishBasketReady`, which is where the missing half belongs.
- `services/asdair/browser-runner/progress.cjs:157` — where `product_count` is recorded and then never checked.
- `services/asdair/browser-runner/RUNNER-PROOF.md` and `README.md` — the runner's own account of its termination behaviour. Read them; report if this change makes either untrue.
- `Deliverables/2026-08-04-build-015-asdair-wayfinder-plan.md` — AC6(f) history. Owner Larry, not yours to edit.

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- Anything outside `browser-runner/`. THREE other workers are live on `bot/**` + `pipeline/runtime.js`, on `pipeline/runPipeline.js` + `deps.js` + control-plane, and on `skill/listNormaliser.js` + `intake/**`. Do not edit their files; report and I will route.
- `handoff/**` and `packet/**` — the producers of the plan you consume. If the real defect is upstream, SAY SO rather than compensating downstream.
- Making the runner more autonomous in any way. Checkout, payment, slot selection and credentials remain absolutely prohibited.
- Repairing or advancing `SHOP-2026-08-09`, which has three live browser requests.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK FIRST, then HOLD** (SOP-022). Restate the outcome, your plan, what the order failed
   to settle, and what looks wrong. State your proposed AC3 line — zero only, or zero plus a
   shortfall rule — and your reasoning. Do not implement until Larry accepts or amends.
2. Measure the browser-runner baseline.
3. AC6 regression FIRST, proven RED against today's runner. That is what proves the defect is real.
4. Implement AC1, then AC2/AC3.
5. AC7 mutation, byte-identical restore.
6. Re-run the suite; report counts.
7. **Git endpoint: COMMIT and PUSH `build-015/b15-12-no-false-basket`. No PR. Do NOT touch `main`.
   Do NOT merge.** Larry integrates and commissions Veritas.

Return: what you changed, both mutation directions with the sha256 pair, suite counts, your AC3
decision and its justification, and anything you refused and why.
